definition: Streaming media refers to media platforms that deliver event content through internet-based and mobile communication systems. In this context, its psychological importance is that the quality of streamed events can influence audience attention and arousal, helping keep viewers engaged and excited.

reasons: The packet supports only a narrow point about streaming media platforms needing high-quality events to keep audiences excited, attention, and arousal; it does not support a general definition of streaming media as media platforms that deliver event content through internet-based and mobile communication systems.
The definition adds a broader psychological/general-media characterization that is not stated in the source packet and goes beyond the supplied evidence.

The definition says streaming media “deliver event content through internet-based and mobile communication systems,” but the packet only mentions “5G mobile communication technology” and “LSES platforms” generally, without clearly stating that streaming media specifically deliver “event content” via internet/mobile communication systems.

The definition’s psychological claim (“quality of streamed events can influence audience attention and arousal…”) is directionally supported by the packet’s statement about the intermediary mechanism of “arousal and attention” and the need to provide “high-quality events,” but because the first sentence contains an unsupported substantive characterization, the definition cannot be fully passed.
